OnCommerce Extends Adyen Partnership to Power Checkout Across easyShop and Comet
summary:
OnCommerce, the marketplace technology company that powers and operates OnBuy, easyShop and Comet, has expanded its partnership with Adyen, the global financial technology platform of choice for leading businesses.
Following the successful rollout of Adyen on OnBuy earlier this year, OnCommerce has now extended the platform across easyShop and Comet. The move brings payments across 43 sites, 21 markets and eight currencies into one system, giving the business a single view of transactions, reporting and reconciliation across all three brands.
The partnership helps simplify operations as OnCommerce continues to scale internationally, while also supporting a smoother checkout experience for customers. With Adyen Protect, transactions are assessed in real time using machine learning and signals from Adyen’s global payments network, helping identify legitimate shoppers more accurately, reduce fraud and minimise unnecessary friction during checkout.
Adyen also gives OnCommerce greater flexibility as it expands. The platform supports a wide range of local payment methods through a single integration, allowing the business to introduce new ways for customers to pay quickly as it enters new markets.
“Over the past year, we've grown from a single marketplace into a multi-brand retail business serving customers across multiple markets and currencies. As we've expanded, it became increasingly important to bring payments across OnBuy, easyShop and Comet together under one roof," said Cas Paton, Founder & CEO of OnCommerce. "Extending our partnership with Adyen gives us a clearer view of the business, faster reconciliation and the ability to deliver a consistent checkout experience across all three brands. Just as importantly, it gives us the flexibility to keep evolving our payment offering and the foundation to support our next stage of growth."
“Expanding into new markets is a huge opportunity for retailers, but it also brings greater complexity, particularly when it comes to payments. Businesses need technology that can support their growth without making the shopping experience more complicated for customers," said Nicole Olbe, President of EMEA at Adyen. "By bringing payments across OnBuy, easyShop and Comet onto one platform, we’re helping OnCommerce simplify its operations, better understand its customers and introduce the payment methods shoppers prefer in each market. It’s a great example of how the right payments infrastructure can help ambitious businesses scale while delivering a seamless experience for customers.”

title: Red Hat Brings Lightwell Network to Microsoft Marketplace
summary:
Red Hat, the world's leading provider of open source solutions, today announced expanded enterprise access to Lightwell Network through availability in the Microsoft Marketplace, the unified online destination for customers to buy trusted cloud solutions,  AI apps, and agents to meet their business needs. Red Hat customers can now discover and deploy Lightwell Network through Microsoft Marketplace, with streamlined management across Microsoft Azure and other Microsoft products.
By making Lightwell Network available via Microsoft Marketplace, Red Hat is making it easier for customers to access eligible, version-specific remediated open source packages through secured repositories, with signed artifacts and supporting provenance, Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) and vulnerability information as applicable.
Lightwell Network is designed to fit into existing software delivery workflows, allowing organisations to use their current vulnerability scanners, artifact repositories, build systems and deployment processes while consuming available Lightwell-remediated packages through secured repositories. These findings can surface in Microsoft Defender for Cloud, and Azure Policy brings governance to the same pipeline, so security and IT teams get visibility and control without changing how developers work.
The accessibility of Lightwell Network on Microsoft Marketplace builds upon Red Hat’s broader open hybrid cloud portfolio, spanning Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Red Hat OpenShift and Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform. While Lightwell is agnostic of the underlying software platforms, consuming patches at AI-scale velocity requires a modern application pipeline. The Red Hat hybrid cloud portfolio helps bring about this modern stack, with:
Security-enhanced, optimised operating foundation for applications across the hybrid cloud with Red Hat Enterprise Linux.
Red Hat OpenShift accelerates containerised application networking and orchestration on any cloud or on-premises environment, strengthened by consistent operational guardrails.
Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform delivers automated network configuration, policy enforcement and lifecycle management to reduce manual overhead and mitigate risk in complex, heterogeneous systems.

title: Supermicro Ships First All-Flash Storage Servers, Delivering PCIe Gen 6 Performance and Broad Software-Defined Storage Support for AI Training and Inference
summary:
Supercomputing Conference - Supermicro, Inc., an AI, Enterprise, Storage, and 5G/Edge Total IT Solution Provider featuring Data Center Building Block Solutions® (DCBBS), today announced new extensions to the broad portfolio of AMD EPYC based all-flash storage servers. The first systems, now shipping, include the Petascale system powered by the 6th Gen AMD EPYC 9006 Series processors (formerly codenamed "Venice"), with more products to follow as AMD launches new SP8 CPU versions. These are the first storage products supporting the PCIe Gen 6 I/O specification with 100% greater sequential read bandwidth over PCIe Gen 5.
"Expanding AI and HPC workloads require storage that can match the performance of today's CPU and GPU clusters," said Vik Malyala, chief business officer at Supermicro. "With our new all-flash storage servers based on AMD EPYC processors, and the flexibility of the DCBBS architecture, we are delivering improved PCIe Gen 6 bandwidth, high density, and scalable capacity. These platforms can be customized for HPC, AI training, and inference workloads, while providing software-defined storage partners with proven, validated systems they can rely on."
Supermicro will be showing the new Petascale all-flash storage server in booth #4017 at Supercomputing 2026, in Chicago, November 15-20.
The first system in the new family packs exceptional density into a 2U chassis with support for up to 32 E3.S NVMe SSDs—delivering as much as 3.93 PB of capacity with 122 TB drives. Its balanced I/O architecture supports up to four x16 high-performance networking cards, enabling the sustained bandwidth required for AI data lakes, large-scale analytics, and high-throughput storage networking while giving customers the flexibility to optimize for their specific workload and fabric requirements.

content: Supermicro has announced the shipment of its new all-flash storage servers, featuring PCIe Gen 6 performance to support AI training and inference. Powered by AMD EPYC processors, the high-density systems deliver scalable capacity and improved bandwidth for demanding AI and HPC workloads.
